+// switchSegments makes the next segment the active one after the active one ended, writing the
+// held packets of the next one that the active one did not write.
+func (c *captureChain) switchSegments(ctx context.Context, timer *time.Timer) (bool, error) {
+	// the held packets are in the reorder buffer once this returns
+	defer c.capture.out.Release(c)
+
+	ended := c.active
+	if c.stopping && c.next != nil && c.next.started.IsZero() {
+		// the chain is stopping: a follow-up that has not started takes nothing over
+		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
+	}
+	if c.final && c.next == nil {
+		return true, nil
+	}
+
+	if c.next == nil || c.next.started.IsZero() || c.cut == 0 {
+		from := ended.ended
+		if from.IsZero() {
+			from = ended.plannedEnd()
+		}
+		gap := clablabruntime.CaptureGap{
+			Node: c.group.display, Interfaces: c.group.interfaces, From: from,
+			Reason: "the follow-up capture did not overlap the previous one",
+		}
+		if c.next != nil && !c.next.started.IsZero() {
+			gap.To = c.next.started
+		}
+		c.capture.reportGap(gap)
+	}
+
+	if c.next != nil && c.next.done && !c.stopping {
+		// the follow-up already ended (it started too late to take over): keep what it
+		// captured and continue with a fresh segment
+		for _, packet := range c.held {
+			if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
+				return true, err
+			}
+		}
+		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
+	}
+
+	if c.next == nil {
+		if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
+			!time.Now().Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
+			return true, nil
+		}
+		c.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
+		resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
+
+		return false, nil
+	}
+
+	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
+	for _, packet := range c.held {
+		if c.cut != 0 {
+			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut-window {
+				continue
+			}
+			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut+window {
+				key := packetKey(packet)
+				if c.emitted[key] > 0 {
+					c.emitted[key]--
+					continue
+				}
+			}
+		}
+		if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
+			return true, err
+		}
+	}
+
+	c.active, c.next = c.next, nil
+	c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, 0
+	if c.active.done {
+		// the chain is stopping and the follow-up ended before the active one
+		return true, nil
+	}
+	resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
+
+	return false, nil
+}
+
+func resetTimer(timer *time.Timer, d time.Duration) {
+	if !timer.Stop() {
+		select {
+		case <-timer.C:
+		default:
+		}
+	}
+	timer.Reset(d)
+}
+
+// packetKey identifies a packet by its interface and content.
+func packetKey(packet *clabcapture.Packet) uint64 {
+	hash := fnv.New64a()
+	var id [4]byte
+	id[0] = byte(packet.InterfaceID)
+	id[1] = byte(packet.InterfaceID >> 8)
+	_, _ = hash.Write(id[:])
+	_, _ = hash.Write(packet.Data)
+
+	return hash.Sum64()
+}
+
+// start runs one clabwire capture and reports its packets, audit records and end as events.
+func (c *captureChain) start(ctx context.Context, duration time.Duration) *captureSegment {
+	segmentCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
+	stdinReader, stdinWriter := io.Pipe()
+	segment := &captureSegment{
+		index: c.segments, localStart: time.Now(), duration: duration, cancel: cancel,
+		closeStdin: func() { _ = stdinWriter.Close() },
+	}
+	c.segments++
+
+	command := []string{
+		clabwireManager, "node-runtime", "packet-capture",
+		"--nodeName", c.group.location.NodeName,
+		"--format", "pcapng",
+		"--snapLength", strconv.Itoa(c.capture.req.SnapLength),
+		"--duration", duration.String(),
+		clabwireStopOnStdinClose,
+	}
+	for _, name := range c.group.interfaces {
+		command = append(command, "--interface", name)
+	}
+	if c.capture.req.PacketLimit > 0 {
+		remaining := int64(c.capture.req.PacketLimit) - c.capture.out.Written()
+		command = append(command, "--packetLimit",
+			strconv.FormatInt(min(max(remaining, 1), maxClabwirePackets), 10))
+	}
+
+	send := func(event segmentEvent) {
+		event.segment = segment
+		select {
+		case c.events <- event:
+		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
+		}
+	}
+
+	stdoutReader, stdoutWriter := io.Pipe()
+	stderr := &auditLineWriter{send: func(audit *captureAudit) { send(segmentEvent{audit: audit}) }}
+
+	// The exec outlives the segment's context by up to captureStdinCloseGrace: when the segment
+	// ends for any reason (the capture is cancelled or failed, the output failed, or a newer
+	// segment took over), its stdin is closed first so clabwire ends on its own, and the stream
+	// is cut only if it does not.
+	execCtx, cancelExec := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(segmentCtx))
+	execDone := make(chan struct{})
+
+	c.wg.Add(3)
+	readDone := make(chan error, 1)
+	go func() {
+		defer c.wg.Done()
+		readDone <- c.readSegment(stdoutReader, func(packet *clabcapture.Packet) {
+			send(segmentEvent{packet: packet})
+		})
+		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, stdoutReader)
+	}()
+	go func() {
+		defer c.wg.Done()
+		select {
+		case <-execDone:
+			return
+		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
+		}
+		segment.closeStdin()
+		grace := time.NewTimer(captureStdinCloseGrace)
+		defer grace.Stop()
+		select {
+		case <-execDone:
+		case <-grace.C:
+			log.Debug("Capture segment did not end after its stdin closed, cutting the stream",
+				"node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index)
+			cancelExec()
+		}
+	}()
+	go func() {
+		defer c.wg.Done()
+		defer cancel()
+		defer cancelExec()
+
+		err := c.capture.r.execInPodContainer()(execCtx, c.group.location.Namespace,
+			c.group.location.Pod, clabwireContainer, command, stdinReader, stdoutWriter, stderr)
+		close(execDone)
+		// the process ended: release the stdin copy of the exec stream
+		segment.closeStdin()
+		_ = stdoutWriter.Close()
+		readErr := <-readDone
+		stderr.flush()
+		if err == nil && readErr != nil {
+			err = readErr
+		}
+		if err != nil && stderr.text() != "" {
+			if unsupported := unsupportedClabwire(
+				c.group.location,
+				stderr.text(),
+			); unsupported != nil {
+				err = unsupported
+			} else {
+				err = fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", err, stderr.text())
+			}
+		}
+		send(segmentEvent{done: true, err: err})
+	}()
+
+	return segment
+}
+
+// unsupportedClabwire recognizes a clabwire that rejects --stop-on-stdin-close, which every
+// capture passes: its release predates the capture contract the runtime needs.
+func unsupportedClabwire(location clablabruntime.NodeLocation, stderr string) error {
+	if !strings.Contains(stderr, "flag provided but not defined") ||
+		!strings.Contains(stderr, strings.TrimPrefix(clabwireStopOnStdinClose, "-")) {
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	return &unsupportedClabernetesError{reason: fmt.Sprintf(
+		"clabwire in pod %s/%s does not accept packet-capture %s",
+		location.Namespace, location.Pod, clabwireStopOnStdinClose)}
+}
+
+// readSegment checks that a segment's interfaces are the requested ones and passes its packets
+// on with the segment's interface index.
+func (c *captureChain) readSegment(stdout io.Reader, packet func(*clabcapture.Packet)) error {
+	reader := clabcapture.NewReader(stdout)
+	interfaces := 0
+	for {
+		event, err := reader.Next()
+		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
+			return nil
+		}
+		if errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) {
+			// the process was stopped inside a block
+			return nil
+		}
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read the clabwire capture: %w", err)
+		}
+		if event.Interface != nil {
+			if interfaces >= len(c.group.interfaces) ||
+				event.Interface.Name != c.group.interfaces[interfaces] {
+				return fmt.Errorf("clabwire described interface %q, want %s in order",
+					event.Interface.Name, strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, ", "))
+			}
+			interfaces++
+			continue
+		}
+		if event.Packet != nil {
+			packet(event.Packet)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// auditLineWriter parses clabwire's stderr: audit records go to send, other lines are kept for
+// error messages.
+type auditLineWriter struct {
+	send func(*captureAudit)
+
+	mu      sync.Mutex
+	partial []byte
+	other   []string
+}
+
+func (w *auditLineWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
+	w.mu.Lock()
+	w.partial = append(w.partial, data...)
+	var lines [][]byte
+	for {
+		idx := bytes.IndexByte(w.partial, '\n')
+		if idx < 0 {
+			break
+		}
+		lines = append(lines, append([]byte(nil), w.partial[:idx]...))
+		w.partial = w.partial[idx+1:]
+	}
+	w.mu.Unlock()
+
+	for _, line := range lines {
+		w.line(line)
+	}
+
+	return len(data), nil
+}
+
+func (w *auditLineWriter) flush() {
+	w.mu.Lock()
+	line := w.partial
+	w.partial = nil
+	w.mu.Unlock()
+	if len(bytes.TrimSpace(line)) != 0 {
+		w.line(line)
+	}
+}
+
+func (w *auditLineWriter) line(line []byte) {
+	line = bytes.TrimSpace(line)
+	if len(line) == 0 {
+		return
+	}
+
+	var audit captureAudit
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(
+		line,
+		&audit,
+	); err == nil &&
+		audit.SchemaVersion == captureAuditSchema {
+		w.send(&audit)
+		return
+	}
+
+	w.mu.Lock()
+	defer w.mu.Unlock()
+	if len(w.other) < 20 {
+		w.other = append(w.other, string(line))
+	}
+}
+
+func (w *auditLineWriter) text() string {
+	w.mu.Lock()
+	defer w.mu.Unlock()
+
+	return strings.Join(w.other, "; ")
+}

+package clabernetes

+
+// streamPodExec runs a command in a pod container without a terminal and streams its stdout
+// and stderr. A non-nil stdin is attached: when it ends, the process's stdin is closed (the
+// websocket v5 close signal, or a half-closed SPDY stream). A nonzero exit returns a
+// *labruntime.CommandExitError.
+func (r *Runtime) streamPodExec(
+	ctx context.Context,
+	namespace, pod, container string,
+	command []string,
+	stdin io.Reader,
+	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
+) error {
+	execURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().
+		Resource("pods").
+		Name(pod).
+		Namespace(namespace).
+		SubResource("exec").
+		VersionedParams(&corev1.PodExecOptions{
+			Container: container,
+			Command:   command,
+			Stdin:     stdin != nil,
+			Stdout:    stdout != nil,
+			Stderr:    stderr != nil,
+		}, scheme.ParameterCodec).URL()
+
+	executor, err := r.newExecutor(execURL)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+
+	// client-go reports streams cut by a cancelled context through the context's logger; a
+	// capture ends that way on purpose, so it goes to the debug log
+	err = executor.StreamWithContext(withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx),
+		remotecommand.StreamOptions{
+			Stdin:  stdin,
+			Stdout: stdout,
+			Stderr: stderr,
+		})
+
+	var exitErr kubeexec.ExitError
+	if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
+		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: exitErr.ExitStatus()}
+	}
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to execute command in pod %s/%s container %s: %w",
+			namespace, pod, container, err)
+	}
+
+	return nil
+}
+
+// InspectInterfaces lists the capturable link interfaces of the requested nodes, or of every
+// running node, in the shape of `inspect interfaces`: per node (named <lab>-<node> like in
+// inspect), the interface and its alias as clabwire reports them, and the MAC address, index,
+// MTU and operational state read from sysfs in the device container. A node whose device
+// container has no shell reports its interfaces without these attributes.
+func (r *Runtime) InspectInterfaces(
+	ctx context.Context,
+	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
+) ([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error) {
+	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
+		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: req.Nodes, Identity: req.Identity,
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	running := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(locations))
+	for _, location := range locations {
+		if location.Pod == "" {
+			log.Warn("Skipping interface detection of a node that does not run",
+				"node", location.NodeName)
+			continue
+		}
+		running = append(running, location)
+	}
+
+	listed, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, running)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	states := r.sampleInterfaceStates(ctx, running)
+
+	result := make([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, 0, len(running))
+	for _, location := range running {
+		container := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces{
+			ContainerName: req.Name + "-" + location.NodeName,
+			Interfaces:    []*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{},
+		}
+		for _, entry := range listed[location.NodeName] {
+			details := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{
+				InterfaceName:  entry.Interface,
+				InterfaceAlias: entry.Alias,
+				// clabwire realizes every lab link interface as a veth pair
+				InterfaceType: "veth",
+			}
+			if state, ok := states[location.NodeName][entry.Interface]; ok {
+				details.InterfaceMAC = state.MAC
+				details.InterfaceIndex = state.Index
+				details.InterfaceMTU = state.MTU
+				details.InterfaceState = state.OperState
+			}
+			container.Interfaces = append(container.Interfaces, details)
+		}
+		sort.Slice(container.Interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {
+			return container.Interfaces[i].InterfaceName < container.Interfaces[j].InterfaceName
+		})
+		result = append(result, container)
+	}
+	sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool {
+		return result[i].ContainerName < result[j].ContainerName
+	})
+
+	return result, nil
+}
+
+// sampleInterfaceStates reads the sysfs interface attributes of every node's device container,
+// one exec per node, with the script the interface events use.
+func (r *Runtime) sampleInterfaceStates(
+	ctx context.Context,
+	locations []clablabruntime.NodeLocation,
+) map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState {
+	var mu sync.Mutex
+	result := map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState{}
+
+	var wg sync.WaitGroup
+	workers := make(chan struct{}, interfaceSampleWorkers)
+	exec := r.execInPodContainer()
+	for _, location := range locations {
+		wg.Add(1)
+		go func() {
+			defer wg.Done()
+			workers <- struct{}{}
+			defer func() { <-workers }()
+
+			var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
+			err := exec(ctx, location.Namespace, location.Pod, location.Container,
+				[]string{"sh", "-c", interfaceSampleScript}, nil, &stdout, &stderr)
+			if err != nil {
+				log.Debug("Cannot read the interface state of a c9s node",
+					"node", location.NodeName, "error", err)
+				return
+			}
+			_, ifaces, _, err := parseInterfaceSample(stdout.Bytes())
+			if err != nil {
+				log.Debug("Cannot parse the interface state of a c9s node",
+					"node", location.NodeName, "error", err)
+				return
+			}
+
+			byName := make(map[string]c9sIfaceState, len(ifaces))
+			for _, iface := range ifaces {
+				byName[iface.Name] = iface
+			}
+			mu.Lock()
+			result[location.NodeName] = byName
+			mu.Unlock()
+		}()
+	}
+	wg.Wait()
+
+	return result
+}

+
+// fakeClabwire plays clabwire packet-capture and --list-interfaces in the fake pod exec. Every
+// capture process sees the same traffic: one packet per tick on each requested interface,
+// carrying the tick number, stamped with the tick time plus a per-process jitter (clabwire stamps
+// packets when it reads them).
+type fakeClabwire struct {
+	t     *testing.T
+	epoch time.Time
+	tick  time.Duration
+
+	mu       sync.Mutex
+	commands [][]string
+	// processes counts the capture processes started per node
+	processes map[string]int
+
+	// startDelay delays the Started record of the given process index (all nodes).
+	startDelay map[int]time.Duration
+	// firstStartDelay delays the Started record of a node's first process.
+	firstStartDelay map[string]time.Duration
+	// fail makes a process write this audit status and exit 1.
+	fail string
+	// stderrOnly makes a process write this text to stderr and exit 1, like a clabwire that
+	// rejects a flag.
+	stderrOnly string
+	// stampSkew stamps the packets of a node this much earlier, as if its stream reached
+	// containerlab this much later than the others.
+	stampSkew map[string]time.Duration
+	// stdinClosed counts the processes that ended because their stdin closed, per node.
+	stdinClosed map[string]int
+	// written counts the packets written to stdout, per node.
+	written map[string]int
+	// sysfs is the device container's interface sample.
+	sysfs string
+}
+
+func newFakeClabwire(t *testing.T, tick time.Duration) *fakeClabwire {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	return &fakeClabwire{
+		t: t, epoch: time.Now(), tick: tick, processes: map[string]int{},
+		startDelay: map[int]time.Duration{}, stampSkew: map[string]time.Duration{},
+		firstStartDelay: map[string]time.Duration{},
+		stdinClosed:     map[string]int{},
+		written:         map[string]int{},
+	}
+}
+
+func (f *fakeClabwire) exec(
+	ctx context.Context,
+	namespace, pod, container string,
+	command []string,
+	stdin io.Reader,
+	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
+) error {
+	f.mu.Lock()
+	f.commands = append(
+		f.commands,
+		append([]string{namespace + "/" + pod + "/" + container}, command...),
+	)
+	f.mu.Unlock()
+
+	if container != clabwireContainer {
+		_, _ = io.WriteString(stdout, f.sysfs)
+		return nil
+	}
+	if slices.Contains(command, "--list-interfaces") {
+		return json.NewEncoder(stdout).Encode(captureListing[pod])
+	}
+
+	return f.capture(ctx, command, stdin, stdout, stderr)
+}
+
+func flagValues(command []string, name string) []string {
+	var values []string
+	for idx := 0; idx+1 < len(command); idx++ {
+		if command[idx] == name {
+			values = append(values, command[idx+1])
+		}
+	}
+
+	return values
+}
+
+func (f *fakeClabwire) audit(
+	stderr io.Writer,
+	status, node string,
+	interfaces []string,
+	reason string,
+) {
+	record := map[string]any{
+		"schemaVersion": captureAuditSchema, "time": time.Now().UTC(), "operation": "PacketCapture",
+		"status": status, "nodeName": node, "format": "pcapng", "reason": reason,
+	}
+	entries := []map[string]any{}
+	for _, name := range interfaces {
+		entries = append(entries, map[string]any{"name": name})
+	}
+	record["interfaces"] = entries
+	data, _ := json.Marshal(record)
+	_, _ = stderr.Write(append(data, '\n'))
+}
+
+func (f *fakeClabwire) capture(
+	ctx context.Context,
+	command []string,
+	stdin io.Reader,
+	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
+) error {
+	f.mu.Lock()
+	rejected := f.stderrOnly
+	f.mu.Unlock()
+	if rejected != "" {
+		_, _ = io.WriteString(stdout, "Incorrect Usage: "+rejected+"\n\nNAME:\n   manager\n")
+		_, _ = io.WriteString(stderr, rejected+"\n")
+		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: 1}
+	}
+
+	// clabwire ends the capture when stdin closes (--stop-on-stdin-close)
+	if !slices.Contains(command, clabwireStopOnStdinClose) || stdin == nil {
+		f.t.Errorf("capture without stdin and %s: %v", clabwireStopOnStdinClose, command)
+		return fmt.Errorf("no stdin")
+	}
+	stdinClosed := make(chan struct{})
+	go func() {
+		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, stdin)
+		close(stdinClosed)
+	}()
+
+	node := flagValues(command, "--nodeName")[0]
+	interfaces := flagValues(command, "--interface")
+	duration, err := time.ParseDuration(flagValues(command, "--duration")[0])
+	if err != nil {
+		f.t.Errorf("duration: %v", err)
+	}
+	if !slices.Equal(flagValues(command, "--format"), []string{"pcapng"}) {
+		f.t.Errorf("capture without --format pcapng: %v", command)
+	}
+
+	f.mu.Lock()
+	index := f.processes[node]
+	f.processes[node]++
+	delay := f.startDelay[index]
+	if index == 0 {
+		delay += f.firstStartDelay[node]
+	}
+	failure := f.fail
+	skew := f.stampSkew[node]
+	f.mu.Unlock()
+
+	if failure != "" {
+		f.audit(stderr, failure, node, interfaces, "interface \"eth9\" is not uniquely planned")
+		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: 1}
+	}
+
+	select {
+	case <-time.After(delay):
+	case <-ctx.Done():
+		return ctx.Err()
+	case <-stdinClosed:
+		f.audit(stderr, captureAuditStarted, node, interfaces, "")
+		f.audit(stderr, captureAuditSucceeded, node, interfaces, "client closed: stdin reached EOF")
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	writer := clabcapture.NewWriter(stdout)
+	f.audit(stderr, captureAuditStarted, node, interfaces, "")
+	if err := writer.WriteHeader(interfaces, clabcapture.DefaultSnapLength); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+
+	// clabwire's own section header names it
+	end := time.Now().Add(duration)
+	jitter := time.Duration(index%3) * 7 * time.Microsecond
+	next := time.Now().Sub(f.epoch)/f.tick + 1
+	for {
+		at := f.epoch.Add(next * f.tick)
+		if at.After(end) {
+			break
+		}
+		select {
+		case <-ctx.Done():
+			return ctx.Err()
+		case <-stdinClosed:
+			f.mu.Lock()
+			f.stdinClosed[node]++
+			f.mu.Unlock()
+			f.audit(
+				stderr,
+				captureAuditSucceeded,
+				node,
+				interfaces,
+				"client closed: stdin reached EOF",
+			)
+			return nil
+		case <-time.After(time.Until(at)):
+		}
+		for id := range interfaces {
+			data := make([]byte, 64)
+			binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(data[0:], uint64(next))
+			copy(data[8:], node+":"+interfaces[id])
+			if err := writer.WritePacket(uint32(id), &clabcapture.Packet{ //nolint:gosec // small
+				Timestamp: at.Add(jitter - skew).UnixNano(), OriginalLength: 64, Data: data,
+			}); err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+			f.mu.Lock()
+			f.written[node]++
+			f.mu.Unlock()
+		}
+		next++
+	}
+	f.audit(stderr, captureAuditSucceeded, node, interfaces, "")
+
+	return nil
+}
+
+func (f *fakeClabwire) captureCommands() [][]string {
+	f.mu.Lock()
+	defer f.mu.Unlock()
+
+	var result [][]string
+	for _, command := range f.commands {
+		if slices.Contains(command, "packet-capture") &&
+			!slices.Contains(command, "--list-interfaces") {
+			result = append(result, command)
+		}
+	}
+
+	return result
+}

+// parsedCapture is a pcapng stream read back.
+type parsedCapture struct {
+	sections   int
+	interfaces []string
+	packets    []clabcapture.Packet
+}
+
+func parseCapture(t *testing.T, data []byte) parsedCapture {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	reader := clabcapture.NewReader(bytes.NewReader(data))
+	var parsed parsedCapture
+	for {
+		event, err := reader.Next()
+		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
+			break
+		}
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("invalid capture: %v", err)
+		}
+		if event.Interface != nil {
+			if len(parsed.packets) != 0 {
+				t.Fatal("interface description after the first packet")
+			}
+			if event.Interface.TSResol != 9 /* nanoseconds */ {
+				t.Fatalf("interface %s tsresol = %d", event.Interface.Name, event.Interface.TSResol)
+			}
+			parsed.interfaces = append(parsed.interfaces, event.Interface.Name)
+		}
+		if event.Packet != nil {
+			parsed.packets = append(parsed.packets, *event.Packet)
+		}
+	}
+	parsed.sections = reader.Sections()
+
+	return parsed
+}
+
+func packetSequence(packet clabcapture.Packet) uint64 {
+	return binary.BigEndian.Uint64(packet.Data[0:8])
+}
+
+func packetOrigin(packet clabcapture.Packet) string {
+	return strings.TrimRight(string(packet.Data[8:]), "\x00")
+}

+// TestCaptureChainsSegmentsWithoutDuplicatesOrGaps runs captures longer than one segment: every
+// tick must appear exactly once per interface, across every switch.
+func TestCaptureChainsSegmentsWithoutDuplicatesOrGaps(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 4*time.Millisecond)
+	r.captureSegment = 300 * time.Millisecond
+
+	var gaps []clablabruntime.CaptureGap
+	var out bytes.Buffer
+	err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
+		Name: "lab1",
+		Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
+			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
+			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-2"},
+		},
+		Duration: 1300 * time.Millisecond,
+		OnGap:    func(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) { gaps = append(gaps, gap) },
+	}, &out)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if len(gaps) != 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("gaps = %+v", gaps)
+	}
+	if processes := len(clabwire.captureCommands()); processes < 4 {
+		t.Fatalf("capture processes = %d, want a chain of at least 4 segments", processes)
+	}
+
+	parsed := parseCapture(t, out.Bytes())
+	if parsed.sections != 1 || len(parsed.interfaces) != 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("sections = %d, interfaces = %v; want the follow-up headers dropped",
+			parsed.sections, parsed.interfaces)
+	}
+	for id := range uint32(2) {
+		var sequence []uint64
+		for _, packet := range parsed.packets {
+			if packet.InterfaceID == id {
+				sequence = append(sequence, packetSequence(packet))
+			}
+		}
+		if len(sequence) < 200 {
+			t.Fatalf("interface %d has %d packets", id, len(sequence))
+		}
+		slices.Sort(sequence)
+		for idx := 1; idx < len(sequence); idx++ {
+			switch {
+			case sequence[idx] == sequence[idx-1]:
+				t.Fatalf("interface %d: tick %d written twice", id, sequence[idx])
+			case sequence[idx] != sequence[idx-1]+1:
+				t.Fatalf(
+					"interface %d: ticks %d to %d missing",
+					id,
+					sequence[idx-1]+1,
+					sequence[idx]-1,
+				)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}

+// TestCaptureClosesStdinWhenItEnds ends every clabwire process through its stdin, whether the
+// caller cancels the capture or the output fails, so no capture is left running in the pod.
+// TestCaptureWritesWhatItReadWhenTheContextEnds stops a capture while the output is slow and
+// the chains have packets queued: every packet clabwire wrote before it ended is in the file.
+func TestCaptureWritesWhatItReadWhenTheContextEnds(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, time.Millisecond)
+	// without a reorder window, a blocked output blocks the chains
+	r.captureReorderWindow = -1
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	defer cancel()
+
+	out := &gatedWriter{open: make(chan struct{})}
+	go func() {
+		time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
+		out.block()
+		// the segments keep reading while the chains wait for the output
+		time.Sleep(400 * time.Millisecond)
+		cancel()
+		close(out.open)
+	}()
+
+	if err := r.Capture(ctx, clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
+		Name: "lab1",
+		Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
+			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
+			{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
+		},
+	}, out); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+
+	parsed := parseCapture(t, out.bytes())
+	got := map[string]int{}
+	for _, packet := range parsed.packets {
+		node, _, _ := strings.Cut(packetOrigin(packet), ":")
+		got[node]++
+	}
+	clabwire.mu.Lock()
+	defer clabwire.mu.Unlock()
+	for _, node := range []string{"r1", "r2"} {
+		if clabwire.written[node] < 300 || got[node] != clabwire.written[node] {
+			t.Fatalf("%s: clabwire wrote %d packets, the capture has %d", node,
+				clabwire.written[node], got[node])
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// gatedWriter collects writes; once blocked, writes wait until open is closed.
+type gatedWriter struct {
+	open chan struct{}
+
+	mu      sync.Mutex
+	blocked bool
+	data    bytes.Buffer
+}
+
+func (w *gatedWriter) block() {
+	w.mu.Lock()
+	w.blocked = true
+	w.mu.Unlock()
+}
+
+func (w *gatedWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
+	w.mu.Lock()
+	blocked := w.blocked
+	w.mu.Unlock()
+	if blocked {
+		<-w.open
+	}
+	w.mu.Lock()
+	defer w.mu.Unlock()
+
+	return w.data.Write(data)
+}
+
+func (w *gatedWriter) bytes() []byte {
+	w.mu.Lock()
+	defer w.mu.Unlock()
+
+	return w.data.Bytes()
+}

+func TestCaptureClosesStdinWhenItEnds(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	targets := []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
+		{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
+		{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
+	}
+
+	t.Run("cancel", func(t *testing.T) {
+		t.Parallel()
+
+		r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 2*time.Millisecond)
+		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 200*time.Millisecond)
+		defer cancel()
+
+		if err := r.Capture(ctx, clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{Name: "lab1", Targets: targets},
+			io.Discard); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		requireStdinClosedEverywhere(t, clabwire)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("output fails", func(t *testing.T) {
+		t.Parallel()
+
+		r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 2*time.Millisecond)
+		output := &failingWriter{accept: 3}
+		err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
+			Name: "lab1", Targets: targets, Duration: time.Hour,
+		}, output)
+		if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "broken pipe") {
+			t.Fatalf("Capture() = %v, want the write error", err)
+		}
+		requireStdinClosedEverywhere(t, clabwire)
+	})
+}
+
+// failingWriter accepts some writes, then fails like a closed pipe.
+type failingWriter struct {
+	mu     sync.Mutex
+	accept int
+}
+
+func (w *failingWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
+	w.mu.Lock()
+	defer w.mu.Unlock()
+	if w.accept == 0 {
+		return 0, errors.New("write |1: broken pipe")
+	}
+	w.accept--
+
+	return len(data), nil
+}
+
+func requireStdinClosedEverywhere(t *testing.T, clabwire *fakeClabwire) {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	clabwire.mu.Lock()
+	defer clabwire.mu.Unlock()
+	for _, node := range []string{"r1", "r2"} {
+		if clabwire.processes[node] == 0 || clabwire.stdinClosed[node] != clabwire.processes[node] {
+			t.Fatalf("%s: %d processes, %d ended through stdin", node,
+				clabwire.processes[node], clabwire.stdinClosed[node])
+		}
+	}
+}

+// requireTimeOrdered checks that the merged stream's timestamps never decrease.
+func requireTimeOrdered(t *testing.T, packets []clabcapture.Packet) {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	for idx := 1; idx < len(packets); idx++ {
+		if packets[idx].Timestamp < packets[idx-1].Timestamp {
+			t.Fatalf("packet %d (%s) at %d precedes packet %d (%s) at %d", idx,
+				packetOrigin(packets[idx]), packets[idx].Timestamp, idx-1,
+				packetOrigin(packets[idx-1]), packets[idx-1].Timestamp)
+		}
+	}
+}

+// TestCaptureMergesNodesInTimestampOrder merges two nodes whose streams arrive with different
+// delays: r2's packets are stamped 60 ms before they reach containerlab. The reorder window puts
+// them in order; without it they are not.
+func TestCaptureMergesNodesInTimestampOrder(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	for _, reorder := range []bool{true, false} {
+		t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("reorder=%v", reorder), func(t *testing.T) {
+			t.Parallel()
+
+			r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 5*time.Millisecond)
+			clabwire.stampSkew["r2"] = 60 * time.Millisecond
+			if !reorder {
+				r.captureReorderWindow = -1
+			}
+
+			var out bytes.Buffer
+			err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
+				Name: "lab1",
+				Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
+					{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
+					{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
+				},
+				Duration: 500 * time.Millisecond,
+			}, &out)
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+
+			packets := parseCapture(t, out.Bytes()).packets
+			ordered := slices.IsSortedFunc(packets, func(a, b clabcapture.Packet) int {
+				return int(a.Timestamp - b.Timestamp)
+			})
+			if reorder {
+				requireTimeOrdered(t, packets)
+			} else if ordered {
+				t.Fatal("the skewed streams came out ordered without the reorder window")
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// TestCaptureChainsSeveralNodesInOrderWithoutDuplicates chains two nodes with skewed streams and a
+// reorder window shorter than a segment switch:
+// every tick appears exactly once per interface and the merged stream stays in timestamp order
+// across every segment switch, while old segments are ended through stdin at the switch.
+func TestCaptureChainsSeveralNodesInOrderWithoutDuplicates(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 4*time.Millisecond)
+	r.captureSegment = 300 * time.Millisecond
+	// a window shorter than a switch: the chains' holds keep the order across the switches
+	r.captureReorderWindow = 15 * time.Millisecond
+	clabwire.stampSkew["r2"] = 5 * time.Millisecond
+	// r2 switches segments 120 ms after r1, so one chain streams live while the other holds
+	clabwire.firstStartDelay["r2"] = 120 * time.Millisecond
+
+	var gaps []clablabruntime.CaptureGap
+	var out bytes.Buffer
+	err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
+		Name: "lab1",
+		Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
+			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
+			{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
+		},
+		Duration: 1300 * time.Millisecond,
+		OnGap:    func(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) { gaps = append(gaps, gap) },
+	}, &out)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if len(gaps) != 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("gaps = %+v", gaps)
+	}
+
+	parsed := parseCapture(t, out.Bytes())
+	requireTimeOrdered(t, parsed.packets)
+	for id := range uint32(2) {
+		var sequence []uint64
+		for _, packet := range parsed.packets {
+			if packet.InterfaceID == id {
+				sequence = append(sequence, packetSequence(packet))
+			}
+		}
+		slices.Sort(sequence)
+		if len(sequence) < 200 {
+			t.Fatalf("interface %d has %d packets", id, len(sequence))
+		}
+		for idx := 1; idx < len(sequence); idx++ {
+			if sequence[idx] != sequence[idx-1]+1 {
+				t.Fatalf("interface %d: tick %d followed by %d", id, sequence[idx-1], sequence[idx])
+			}
+		}
+	}
+
+	clabwire.mu.Lock()
+	defer clabwire.mu.Unlock()
+	for _, node := range []string{"r1", "r2"} {
+		if clabwire.processes[node] < 4 || clabwire.stdinClosed[node] == 0 {
+			t.Fatalf("%s: %d processes, %d stopped through stdin at a switch", node,
+				clabwire.processes[node], clabwire.stdinClosed[node])
+		}
+	}
+}

+func TestCaptureReorderWindowKnob(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := map[string]time.Duration{
+		"":      250 * time.Millisecond,
+		"0":     0,
+		"75ms":  75 * time.Millisecond,
+		"bogus": 250 * time.Millisecond,
+	}
+	for value, want := range cases {
+		t.Setenv(envCaptureReorderWindow, value)
+		r := &Runtime{captureReorderWindow: captureReorderWindowFromEnv()}
+		if got := r.captureReorderWindowLength(); got != want {
+			t.Errorf("%s=%q: window %s, want %s", envCaptureReorderWindow, value, got, want)
+		}
+	}
+}

6502: +
6503: +Prints the number of sections, the interface names in order, the packet count per interface,
6504: +whether packets are in timestamp order, the number of 802.1Q tagged frames and the number of
6505: +ICMP echo requests and replies (untagged or tagged).
6506: +"""

6508: +import json
6509: +import struct
6510: +import sys
6511: +
6512: +SHB, IDB, EPB = 0x0A0D0D0A, 0x00000001, 0x00000006
6513: +
6514: +
6515: +def main(path):
6516: +    with open(path, "rb") as f:
6517: +        data = f.read()
6518: +
6519: +    sections, names, counts, stamps = 0, [], {}, []
6520: +    vlan, echo = 0, 0
6521: +    offset = 0
6522: +    while offset < len(data):
6523: +        block_type, length = struct.unpack_from("<II", data, offset)
6524: +        body = data[offset + 8 : offset + length - 4]
6525: +        if block_type == SHB:
6526: +            sections += 1
6527: +        elif block_type == IDB:
6528: +            options, name = body[8:], ""
6529: +            while len(options) >= 4:
6530: +                code, size = struct.unpack_from("<HH", options)
6531: +                if code == 0:
6532: +                    break
6533: +                if code == 2:
6534: +                    name = options[4 : 4 + size].decode()
6535: +                options = options[4 + size + (4 - size % 4) % 4 :]
6536: +            names.append(name)
6537: +        elif block_type == EPB:
6538: +            iface, high, low, captured = struct.unpack_from("<IIII", body)
6539: +            frame = body[20 : 20 + captured]
6540: +            counts[names[iface]] = counts.get(names[iface], 0) + 1
6541: +            stamps.append(high << 32 | low)
6542: +            ethertype, l3 = struct.unpack_from(">H", frame, 12)[0], 14
6543: +            if ethertype == 0x8100:
6544: +                vlan += 1
6545: +                ethertype, l3 = struct.unpack_from(">H", frame, 16)[0], 18
6546: +            if ethertype == 0x0800 and frame[l3 + 9] == 1 and frame[l3 + 20] in (0, 8):

6554: +                "interfaces": names,
6555: +                "packets": counts,
6556: +                "ordered": stamps == sorted(stamps),
6557: +                "vlan_frames": vlan,
6558: +                "icmp_echo": echo,
6559: +            }

6984: +#!/bin/sh
6985: +# Prints the packet-capture processes running in the clabwire container of a c9s node's pod.
6986: +# usage: clabwire-captures.sh <namespace> <node>
6987: +#
6988: +# A process of a Kubernetes exec is not visible through the API, so this looks at the worker
6989: +# that runs the pod: a KinD node, which is a Docker container. It lists the processes whose
6990: +# cgroup belongs to the clabwire container. Exits 2 when the worker is not a Docker container.
6991: +set -eu
6992: +
6993: +namespace=$1
6994: +node=$2
6995: +
6996: +pod=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod -l "c9s.run/topologyNode=$node" \
6997: +  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
6998: +worker=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}')
6999: +# clabwire is a sidecar (an init container that keeps running)
7000: +container=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath=\
7001: +'{.status.initContainerStatuses[?(@.name=="clabwire")].containerID}{.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="clabwire")].containerID}')

7011: +fi

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# Copyright 2020 Nokia
+# Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
+"""Summarize a little-endian pcapng file as containerlab capture writes it, as JSON.
+
+Prints the number of sections, the interface names in order, the packet count per interface,
+whether packets are in timestamp order, the number of 802.1Q tagged frames and the number of
+ICMP echo requests and replies (untagged or tagged).
+"""
+
+import json
+import struct
+import sys
+
+SHB, IDB, EPB = 0x0A0D0D0A, 0x00000001, 0x00000006
+
+
+def main(path):
+    with open(path, "rb") as f:
+        data = f.read()
+
+    sections, names, counts, stamps = 0, [], {}, []
+    vlan, echo = 0, 0
+    offset = 0
+    while offset < len(data):
+        block_type, length = struct.unpack_from("<II", data, offset)
+        body = data[offset + 8 : offset + length - 4]
+        if block_type == SHB:
+            sections += 1
+        elif block_type == IDB:
+            options, name = body[8:], ""
+            while len(options) >= 4:
+                code, size = struct.unpack_from("<HH", options)
+                if code == 0:
+                    break
+                if code == 2:
+                    name = options[4 : 4 + size].decode()
+                options = options[4 + size + (4 - size % 4) % 4 :]
+            names.append(name)
+        elif block_type == EPB:
+            iface, high, low, captured = struct.unpack_from("<IIII", body)
+            frame = body[20 : 20 + captured]
+            counts[names[iface]] = counts.get(names[iface], 0) + 1
+            stamps.append(high << 32 | low)
+            ethertype, l3 = struct.unpack_from(">H", frame, 12)[0], 14
+            if ethertype == 0x8100:
+                vlan += 1
+                ethertype, l3 = struct.unpack_from(">H", frame, 16)[0], 18
+            if ethertype == 0x0800 and frame[l3 + 9] == 1 and frame[l3 + 20] in (0, 8):
+                echo += 1
+        offset += length
+
+    print(
+        json.dumps(
+            {
+                "sections": sections,
+                "interfaces": names,
+                "packets": counts,
+                "ordered": stamps == sorted(stamps),
+                "vlan_frames": vlan,
+                "icmp_echo": echo,
+            }
+        )
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main(sys.argv[1])

+#!/bin/sh
+# Prints the packet-capture processes running in the clabwire container of a c9s node's pod.
+# usage: clabwire-captures.sh <namespace> <node>
+#
+# A process of a Kubernetes exec is not visible through the API, so this looks at the worker
+# that runs the pod: a KinD node, which is a Docker container. It lists the processes whose
+# cgroup belongs to the clabwire container. Exits 2 when the worker is not a Docker container.
+set -eu
+
+namespace=$1
+node=$2
+
+pod=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod -l "c9s.run/topologyNode=$node" \
+  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
+worker=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}')
+# clabwire is a sidecar (an init container that keeps running)
+container=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath=\
+'{.status.initContainerStatuses[?(@.name=="clabwire")].containerID}{.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="clabwire")].containerID}')
+container=${container#*://}
+
+if ! docker inspect --type container "$worker" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo "worker $worker of pod $namespace/$pod is not a Docker container (KinD)" >&2
+  exit 2
+fi
+if [ -z "$container" ]; then
+  echo "pod $namespace/$pod has no running clabwire container" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+docker exec "$worker" sh -c "
+  for proc in /proc/[0-9]*; do
+    if grep -qs '$container' \"\$proc/cgroup\"; then
+      tr '\\0' ' ' < \"\$proc/cmdline\" 2>/dev/null && echo
+    fi
+  done" | grep 'packet-capture' || true

145: 		return err
146: 	}

148: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup

150: 		reader := &localReader{
151: 			capture: l,
152: 			out:     out,
153: 			id:      uint32(idx), //nolint:gosec // bounded by the targets

171: 	targets []LocalTarget,
172: 	snapLength int,

178: 	}

182: 		group := byNode[target.Node]

185: 			byNode[target.Node] = group
186: 			order = append(order, target.Node)
187: 		}
188: 		group.indexes = append(group.indexes, idx)
189: 		group.names = append(group.names, target.Interface)
190: 	}
191: 
192: 	sources := make([]packetSource, len(targets))

194: 		for _, source := range sources {
195: 			if source != nil {
196: 				source.Close()
197: 			}
198: 		}
199: 	}
200: 	for _, node := range order {
201: 		group := byNode[node]
202: 		opened, err := l.open(ctx, group.exec, group.names, snapLength)
203: 		if err != nil {
204: 			closeAll()

217: 	capture localCapture
218: 	out     *Output
219: 	id      uint32

226: 	defer func() {
227: 		if source != nil {
228: 			source.Close()
229: 		}
230: 	}()
231: 
232: 	for {
233: 		if ctx.Err() != nil {
234: 			r.drain(source, time.Now())
235: 			return
236: 		}
237: 
238: 		data, info, err := source.ReadPacket()
239: 		if errors.Is(err, errReadTimeout) {
240: 			continue
241: 		}
242: 		if err != nil {
243: 			// The socket reports an error once its interface went down or was removed, and
244: 			// keeps reporting it: it is reopened.

247: 			source.Close()
248: 			source = r.reopen(ctx)
249: 			if source == nil {
250: 				return
251: 			}
252: 
253: 			continue
254: 		}
255: 
256: 		if more, err := r.out.Emit(r.id, r.packet(data, info)); !more || err != nil {
257: 			return
258: 		}
259: 	}
260: }

262: // drain writes the packets that arrived before end but were still in the socket's ring: the

264: // packets before a capture ended may not have been read yet.
265: func (r *localReader) drain(source packetSource, end time.Time) {
266: 	deadline := end.Add(localDrainTimeout)
267: 	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
268: 		data, info, err := source.ReadPacket()
269: 		if errors.Is(err, errReadTimeout) && time.Since(end) < localDrainQuiet {
270: 			continue
271: 		}
272: 		if err != nil || info.Timestamp.After(end) {
273: 			return
274: 		}
275: 		if more, err := r.out.Emit(r.id, r.packet(data, info)); !more || err != nil {
276: 			return
277: 		}
278: 	}
279: }

281: // packet copies a packet out of the socket's ring, cut to the snap length.

283: 	length := info.Length
284: 	for _, ancillary := range info.AncillaryData {
285: 		if _, ok := ancillary.(afpacket.AncillaryVLAN); ok {
286: 			// the tag was put back into the data and counts toward the frame length
287: 			length += vlanHeaderLength

289: 		}
290: 	}

293: 	captured := make([]byte, min(len(data), r.snap))
294: 	copy(captured, data)
295: 
296: 	return &Packet{
297: 		Timestamp:      info.Timestamp.UnixNano(),
298: 		OriginalLength: uint32(length), //nolint:gosec // bounded by the interface MTU
299: 		Data:           captured,
300: 	}
301: }
302: 
303: // reopen opens the interface's socket again once its node and interface are back. It returns
304: // nil when the capture ended first. Time the interface could not be opened is reported as a gap;
305: // an interface that only went down is not, as it has no traffic while down.
306: func (r *localReader) reopen(ctx context.Context) packetSource {
307: 	from := time.Now()
308: 	var unavailable error
309: 
310: 	timer := time.NewTimer(r.capture.reopenInterval)
311: 	defer timer.Stop()
312: 
313: 	for {
314: 		select {
315: 		case <-ctx.Done():
316: 			if unavailable != nil {
317: 				r.reportGap(from, time.Time{}, unavailable)
318: 			}
319: 
320: 			return nil
321: 		case <-timer.C:
322: 		}
323: 
324: 		opened, err := r.capture.open(ctx, r.target.Exec, []string{r.target.Interface}, r.snap)
325: 		if err != nil {
326: 			if unavailable == nil {
327: 				log.Debug("Capture interface is not available, waiting for it",
328: 					"node", r.target.Node, "interface", r.target.Interface, "error", err)
329: 			}
330: 			unavailable = err
331: 			resetTimer(timer, r.capture.reopenInterval)
332: 
333: 			continue
334: 		}
335: 		if unavailable != nil {
336: 			r.reportGap(from, time.Now(), unavailable)
337: 		}
338: 
339: 		return opened[0]
340: 	}
341: }
342: 
343: func (r *localReader) reportGap(from, to time.Time, cause error) {
344: 	ReportGap(r.onGap, clablabruntime.CaptureGap{
345: 		Node:       r.target.Node,
346: 		Interfaces: []string{r.target.Interface},
347: 		From:       from,
348: 		To:         to,
349: 		Reason:     fmt.Sprintf("the interface was not available: %v", cause),
350: 	})
351: }
352: 
353: // openPacketSockets opens one packet socket per interface in the namespace exec enters. A socket
354: // stays bound to its interface after the thread left the namespace.
355: func openPacketSockets(
356: 	ctx context.Context,
357: 	exec ExecFunc,
358: 	interfaces []string,
359: 	snapLength int,
360: ) ([]packetSource, error) {
361: 	sources := make([]packetSource, 0, len(interfaces))
362: 	err := exec(ctx, func(ns.NetNS) error {
363: 		for _, name := range interfaces {
364: 			source, err := openPacketSocket(name, snapLength)
365: 			if err != nil {
366: 				return fmt.Errorf("interface %q: %w", name, err)
367: 			}
368: 			sources = append(sources, source)
369: 		}
370: 
371: 		return nil
372: 	})
373: 	if err != nil {
374: 		for _, source := range sources {
375: 			source.Close()
376: 		}
377: 
378: 		return nil, err
379: 	}
380: 
381: 	return sources, nil
382: }
383: 
384: // afpacketSource is a TPACKET_V3 receive ring on one interface.
385: type afpacketSource struct {
386: 	handle *afpacket.TPacket
387: }
388: 
389: func openPacketSocket(name string, snapLength int) (*afpacketSource, error) {
390: 	// A TPACKET_V3 block holds whole frames: it must be larger than the snap length, plus the
391: 	// block and frame headers, and a multiple of the page size.
392: 	pageSize := os.Getpagesize()
393: 	blockSize := max(localMinBlockSize, snapLength+pageSize)
394: 	blockSize = (blockSize + pageSize - 1) / pageSize * pageSize
395: 
396: 	handle, err := afpacket.NewTPacket(
397: 		afpacket.OptInterface(name),
398: 		afpacket.OptTPacketVersion(afpacket.TPacketVersion3),
399: 		afpacket.OptFrameSize(blockSize),
400: 		afpacket.OptBlockSize(blockSize),
401: 		afpacket.OptNumBlocks(localRingBlocks),
402: 		afpacket.OptBlockTimeout(localBlockTimeout),
403: 		afpacket.OptPollTimeout(localPollTimeout),
404: 		// the kernel moves 802.1Q tags out of the frame; captures show them in place
405: 		afpacket.OptAddVLANHeader(true),
406: 	)
407: 	if err != nil {
408: 		return nil, err
409: 	}
410: 	// promiscuous mode is a membership of this socket and ends with it
411: 	if err := handle.SetPromiscuous(true); err != nil {
412: 		handle.Close()
413: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to enable promiscuous mode: %w", err)
414: 	}
415: 
416: 	return &afpacketSource{handle: handle}, nil
417: }

423: 	}
424: 
425: 	return data, info, err

13: // are written early, which can put them out of order.
14: const maxReorderBytes = 64 << 20
15: 
16: // Reorder writes the packets of several capture sources in timestamp order.
17: //
18: // Each source (a node's capture stream, or a local interface socket) delivers its packets with
19: // its own delay. The buffer holds every packet for `window` after it arrived and writes the held
20: // packets in timestamp order, so a packet that was stamped earlier but delivered up to `window`
21: // later still goes out first. A packet stamped before the last packet written arrived too late
22: // to be ordered: it is written as it comes and counted, and the count goes to the debug log when
23: // the capture ends.
24: //
25: // A source can place a hold at the earliest timestamp it may still write (Hold); packets stamped
26: // after a hold wait for it to be released (Release). The c9s runtime holds while it switches
27: // between chained capture segments.
28: type Reorder struct {
29: 	write  func(id uint32, packet *Packet) error
30: 	onFail func()
31: 	window time.Duration
32: 	now    func() time.Time
33: 
34: 	mu     sync.Mutex
35: 	queue  reorderQueue
36: 	bytes  int
37: 	seq    uint64
38: 	holds  map[any]int64
39: 	err    error

41: 	stats  reorderStats
42: 	cursor int64 // timestamp of the latest packet written in order

45: type reorderStats struct {

51: // reorderedPacket is a packet waiting in the buffer.

55: 	arrived time.Time

64: func (q reorderQueue) Less(i, j int) bool {
65: 	if q[i].packet.Timestamp != q[j].packet.Timestamp {
66: 		return q[i].packet.Timestamp < q[j].packet.Timestamp
67: 	}

69: 	return q[i].seq < q[j].seq

104: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
105: 
106: 	if q.err != nil {
107: 		return q.err
108: 	}

73: 	return p.sections
74: }
75: 
76: // Event is one block of interest: a new interface or a packet.
77: type Event struct {
78: 	Interface *InterfaceDescription
79: 	Packet    *Packet
80: }
81: 
82: // Next returns the next interface or packet, skipping other block types. It returns io.EOF at
83: // the clean end of the stream, and io.ErrUnexpectedEOF for a stream cut inside a block.
84: func (p *Reader) Next() (Event, error) {
85: 	for {
86: 		var header [8]byte
87: 		if _, err := io.ReadFull(p.r, header[:]); err != nil {
88: 			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
89: 				return Event{}, io.EOF
90: 			}
91: 
92: 			return Event{}, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF
93: 		}
94: 
95: 		blockType := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(header[0:4])
96: 		length := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(header[4:8])
97: 		if blockType == pcapngSectionHeaderType {
98: 			// the byte-order magic tells a big-endian section apart before its length is
99: 			// trusted: that length reads byte swapped
100: 			magic, err := p.r.Peek(4)
101: 			if err != nil {
102: 				return Event{}, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF
103: 			}
104: 			if binary.BigEndian.Uint32(magic) == pcapngByteOrderMagic {
105: 				return Event{}, errPCAPNGByteOrder
106: 			}
107: 		}
108: 		if length < 12 || length%4 != 0 || length > pcapngMaxBlockLength {
109: 			return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid pcapng block length %d (at most %d)", length,
110: 				pcapngMaxBlockLength)
111: 		}
112: 
113: 		body := make([]byte, length-8)
114: 		if _, err := io.ReadFull(p.r, body); err != nil {
115: 			return Event{}, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF
116: 		}
117: 		if binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[len(body)-4:]) != length {
118: 			return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng block lengths do not match")
119: 		}
120: 		body = body[:len(body)-4]
121: 
122: 		switch blockType {
123: 		case pcapngSectionHeaderType:
124: 			if len(body) < 16 {
125: 				return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("short pcapng section header")
126: 			}
127: 			if binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[0:4]) != pcapngByteOrderMagic {
128: 				return Event{}, errPCAPNGByteOrder
129: 			}
130: 			p.sections++
131: 			p.interfaces = nil
132: 		case pcapngInterfaceType:
133: 			if p.sections == 0 {
134: 				return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng interface before a section header")
135: 			}
136: 			intf, err := parsePCAPNGInterface(body)
137: 			if err != nil {
138: 				return Event{}, err
139: 			}
140: 			p.interfaces = append(p.interfaces, intf)
141: 
142: 			return Event{Interface: &p.interfaces[len(p.interfaces)-1]}, nil
143: 		case pcapngEnhancedPacketType:
144: 			packet, err := p.parsePacket(body)
145: 			if err != nil {
146: 				return Event{}, err
147: 			}
148: 
149: 			return Event{Packet: &packet}, nil
150: 		}
151: 	}
152: }
153: 
154: func parsePCAPNGInterface(body []byte) (InterfaceDescription, error) {
155: 	if len(body) < 8 {
156: 		return InterfaceDescription{}, fmt.Errorf("short pcapng interface description")
157: 	}
158: 	intf := InterfaceDescription{
159: 		LinkType:   binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(body[0:2]),
160: 		SnapLength: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[4:8]),
161: 		TSResol:    6,
162: 	}
163: 
164: 	options := body[8:]
165: 	for len(options) >= 4 {
166: 		code := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(options[0:2])
167: 		size := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(options[2:4]))
168: 		if code == pcapngOptionEnd {
169: 			break
170: 		}
171: 		padded := size + pcapngPadding(size)
172: 		if 4+padded > len(options) {
173: 			return InterfaceDescription{}, fmt.Errorf("truncated pcapng interface option")
174: 		}
175: 		value := options[4 : 4+size]
176: 		switch code {
177: 		case pcapngOptionIfName:
178: 			intf.Name = string(value)
179: 		case pcapngOptionIfTSResol:
180: 			if size == 1 {
181: 				intf.TSResol = value[0]
182: 			}
183: 		}
184: 		options = options[4+padded:]
185: 	}
186: 
187: 	return intf, nil
188: }
189: 
190: func (p *Reader) parsePacket(body []byte) (Packet, error) {
191: 	if len(body) < 20 {
192: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("short pcapng enhanced packet")
193: 	}
194: 	packet := Packet{
195: 		InterfaceID:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[0:4]),
196: 		OriginalLength: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[16:20]),
197: 	}
198: 	if int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(p.interfaces) {
199: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng packet for undeclared interface %d",
200: 			packet.InterfaceID)
201: 	}
202: 	captured := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[12:16])
203: 	if int(captured) > len(body)-20 {
204: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng packet data exceeds its block")
205: 	}
206: 	packet.Data = body[20 : 20+captured]
207: 
208: 	raw := uint64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[4:8]))<<32 |
209: 		uint64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[8:12]))
210: 	timestamp, err := pcapngNanosecondsFrom(raw, p.interfaces[packet.InterfaceID].TSResol)
211: 	if err != nil {
212: 		return Packet{}, err
213: 	}
214: 	packet.Timestamp = timestamp
215: 
216: 	return packet, nil
217: }
218: 
219: // pcapngNanosecondsFrom converts a timestamp in an interface's resolution to nanoseconds.
220: // Only decimal resolutions up to nanoseconds occur in clabwire streams.
221: func pcapngNanosecondsFrom(raw uint64, tsresol byte) (int64, error) {
222: 	if tsresol&0x80 != 0 || tsresol > pcapngNanoseconds {
223: 		return 0, fmt.Errorf("unsupported pcapng timestamp resolution %#x", tsresol)
224: 	}
225: 	scale := uint64(1)
226: 	for range pcapngNanoseconds - int(tsresol) {
227: 		scale *= 10
228: 	}
229: 	if raw > math.MaxInt64/scale {
230: 		return 0, fmt.Errorf("pcapng timestamp out of range")
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	return int64(raw * scale), nil //nolint:gosec // bounded above
234: }
235: 
236: // Writer writes one little-endian section with nanosecond timestamps. Every block goes out
237: // in one Write under a lock, so concurrent writers never interleave blocks and a stream cut
238: // between writes is still a valid capture.
239: type Writer struct {
240: 	mu  sync.Mutex
241: 	w   io.Writer
242: 	err error
243: }
244: 
245: // NewWriter returns a writer of one pcapng section to w.
246: func NewWriter(w io.Writer) *Writer {
247: 	return &Writer{w: w}
248: }
249: 
250: // WriteHeader writes the Section Header Block and one Interface Description Block per name, in
251: // order; packets refer to the interfaces by that index.
252: func (p *Writer) WriteHeader(names []string, snapLength uint32) error {
253: 	section := make([]byte, 16)
254: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(section[0:], pcapngByteOrderMagic)
255: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(section[4:], 1)
256: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(section[6:], 0)
257: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(section[8:], math.MaxUint64)
258: 	section = appendPCAPNGOption(section, pcapngOptionUserAppl, []byte(captureUserApplication))
259: 	section = appendPCAPNGOption(section, pcapngOptionEnd, nil)
260: 
261: 	header := pcapngBlock(pcapngSectionHeaderType, section)
262: 	for _, name := range names {
263: 		description := make([]byte, 8)
264: 		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(description[0:], pcapngLinkTypeEthernet)
265: 		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(description[4:], snapLength)
266: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionIfName, []byte(name))
267: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionIfTSResol,
268: 			[]byte{pcapngNanoseconds})
269: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionEnd, nil)
270: 		header = append(header, pcapngBlock(pcapngInterfaceType, description)...)
271: 	}
272: 
273: 	return p.write(header)
274: }
275: 
276: // WritePacket writes an Enhanced Packet Block for the interface with the given index.
277: func (p *Writer) WritePacket(interfaceID uint32, packet *Packet) error {
278: 	timestamp := uint64(packet.Timestamp) //nolint:gosec // capture timestamps are positive
279: 	body := make([]byte, 20, 20+len(packet.Data)+3)
280: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[0:], interfaceID)
281: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[4:], uint32(timestamp>>32))
282: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[8:], uint32(timestamp)) //nolint:gosec // low 32 bits
283: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[12:], uint32(len(packet.Data)))
284: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[16:], packet.OriginalLength)
285: 	body = append(body, packet.Data...)
286: 	body = append(body, make([]byte, pcapngPadding(len(packet.Data)))...)
287: 
288: 	return p.write(pcapngBlock(pcapngEnhancedPacketType, body))
289: }
290: 
291: // Err returns the first write error, or nil.
292: func (p *Writer) Err() error {
293: 	p.mu.Lock()
294: 	defer p.mu.Unlock()
295: 
296: 	return p.err
297: }
298: 
299: func (p *Writer) write(block []byte) error {
300: 	p.mu.Lock()
301: 	defer p.mu.Unlock()
302: 
303: 	if p.err != nil {
304: 		return p.err
305: 	}
306: 	if _, err := p.w.Write(block); err != nil {
307: 		p.err = fmt.Errorf("failed to write the capture: %w", err)
308: 	}
309: 
310: 	return p.err
311: }
312: 
313: func pcapngBlock(blockType uint32, body []byte) []byte {
314: 	total := uint32(12 + len(body)) //nolint:gosec // bounded by the snap length
315: 	block := make([]byte, 8, total)
316: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(block[0:], blockType)
317: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(block[4:], total)
318: 	block = append(block, body...)
319: 
320: 	return binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint32(block, total)
321: }
322: 
323: func appendPCAPNGOption(body []byte, code uint16, value []byte) []byte {
324: 	body = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint16(body, code)
325: 	body = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint16(body, uint16(len(value))) //nolint:gosec // short
326: 	body = append(body, value...)
327: 
328: 	return append(body, make([]byte, pcapngPadding(len(value)))...)
329: }
330: 
331: func pcapngPadding(length int) int {
332: 	return (4 - length%4) % 4
333: }

Notable observations so far:

1. `capture/local.go` `drain()`: after ctx done, drain reads with `time.Now().Before(deadline)` — but ReadPacket can block up to localPollTimeout (100ms), deadline is end+250ms. Potential issue: `drain` loops calling `source.ReadPacket()` — if source returns errReadTimeout after `localDrainQuiet` it returns. OK.

2. `localReader.run`: on ctx done, drain; but note when `r.out.Emit` returns `!more` (packet limit reached), reader returns without drain — fine.

3. `Output.Emit`: increments `written` before push; if `reorder.Push` fails, count already added. Minor.

4. `Reorder.Push` with cursor: `q.cursor != 0 && packet.Timestamp < q.cursor` — late packets written out of order. Note `cursor` only updated in popLocked. `writeLocked` direct writes don't update cursor... Actually in Push, late packet writeLocked does not update cursor — but late packet is behind cursor already, fine.

5. `Reorder.writeDue` holds: computes min timestamp among holds; packets with Timestamp > limit wait. OK.

6. `Output.Close` calls cancelRun then waits, then Flush — but Flush writes remaining packets ignoring holds (flushes all). Good.

7. Potential deadlock in local.go `run`: readers exit when `Emit` returns false... after stop() called (packet limit), sources still open; readers return. wg.Wait. Fine.

8. `drain` deadline: `deadline := end.Add(localDrainTimeout)`; loop condition `time.Now().Before(deadline)`; inside, if errReadTimeout && time.Since(end) < localDrainQuiet → continue; but if time.Since(end) >= localDrainQuiet and errReadTimeout, falls to `if err != nil || ...` → return. OK.

9. In `drain`, `info.Timestamp.After(end)` returns, dropping packets stamped after end — reasonable.

10. capture/local.go reopen: after ctx done reports gap with To zero. OK.

Potential bug: In `localCapture.run`, when `NewOutput` fails, closes sources and returns — but the `captureCtx` cancel timers are deferred, fine.

Potential issue: `openAll` — if `l.open` returns fewer sources than `len(group.names)`? e.g., opened has len != len(names); mapping `sources[group.indexes[idx]]` would panic index out of range if opened shorter, or leave nil entries if longer. openPacketSockets appends one per interface, so equal in practice. Minor.

11. pcapng.go `Next`: peek of 4 bytes for byte-order magic at SHB — if the peek fails with EOF returns ErrUnexpectedEOF even when it's a clean EOF (truncated section header at end). Minor.

12. Writer.WriteHeader: section header block: `section := make([]byte, 16)`, puts magic at 0, major 4, minor 6, section length 8..16 math.MaxUint64. Correct per spec.

13. `pcapngBlock` — total = 12+len(body). Block = 4 type + 4 length + body + 4 total. Good.

14. appendPCAPNGOption padding: appends value then padding of len(value) — correct.

15. `WritePacket` timestamp: `uint64(packet.Timestamp)` — if Timestamp negative (pre-1970), wraps. nolint noted. Minor.

16. Reorder.Run wait computation: `next.Sub(q.now())` could be negative? It computes max(..., time.Millisecond). OK.

17. `resetTimer` — standard.

113: func captureFn(cmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {

163: 	if file, ok := output.(*os.File); ok && output != cmd.OutOrStdout() {
164: 		if err := file.Sync(); err != nil {

188: 		for _, name := range strings.Split(interfaces, ",") {

192: 			}

195: 	}

243: 	table := tableWriter.NewWriter()

249: 	table.SetColumnConfigs([]tableWriter.ColumnConfig{{Number: 1, AutoMerge: true}})

255: 		table.AppendRow(tableWriter.Row{

447: // Capture streams pcapng from lab link interfaces to w: one section, one Interface Description
448: // Block per target in request order named <node>:<interface>, then the packets of every target.
449: //
450: // Each node's interfaces are captured by one clabwire process in the node's pod. clabwire limits
451: // a capture to one hour, so a longer capture (or one without Duration) chains captures: the next
452: // one starts before the current one ends, and the stream switches at a cut in the overlap. See
453: // captureChain for how packets of the overlap are kept once.
454: //
455: // Packets go out in timestamp order across nodes, through a reorder buffer (captureReorder).
456: //
457: // Every clabwire process runs with stdin attached and --stop-on-stdin-close: a Kubernetes exec
458: // does not stop its process when the stream closes, so containerlab closes stdin whenever a
459: // segment ends (the capture ends, fails, its output fails, or a newer segment took over) and
460: // clabwire ends the capture itself.
461: //
462: // Capture returns when Duration has passed, PacketLimit packets were written, or ctx ends; an
463: // ended ctx is not an error. Every block reaches w in one write, so the stream is a valid capture
464: // whenever it stops. A clabwire Denied or Failed audit record is returned as an error.
465: func (r *Runtime) Capture(
466: 	ctx context.Context,
467: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
468: 	w io.Writer,
469: ) error {
470: 	if err := clabcapture.ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {
471: 		return err
472: 	}
473: 
474: 	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
475: 	if err != nil {
476: 		return err
477: 	}
478: 
479: 	resolved, err := r.resolveCaptureTargets(ctx, req)
480: 	if err != nil {
481: 		return err
482: 	}
483: 
484: 	captureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)
485: 	defer stop()
486: 
487: 	out, err := clabcapture.NewOutput(w, resolved.names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit,
488: 		r.captureReorderWindowLength(), stop)
489: 	if err != nil {
490: 		return err
491: 	}
492: 
493: 	run := &captureRun{
494: 		r:       r,
495: 		req:     req,
496: 		out:     out,
497: 		segment: r.captureSegmentLength(),
498: 	}
499: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
500: 		run.deadline = time.Now().Add(req.Duration)
501: 	}
502: 	run.overlap = min(maxCaptureOverlap, run.segment/3)
503: 	run.window = min(maxCaptureCutWindow, run.overlap/4)
504: 
505: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
506: 		// a clabwire process that does not end on its own does not hold the capture open
507: 		var cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc
508: 		captureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx,
509: 			req.Duration+run.overlap+captureEndGrace)
510: 		defer cancelTimeout()
511: 	}
512: 
513: 	group, groupCtx := errgroup.WithContext(captureCtx)
514: 	for _, captureGroup := range resolved.groups {
515: 		chain := &captureChain{capture: run, group: captureGroup}
516: 		group.Go(func() error {
517: 			return chain.run(groupCtx)
518: 		})
519: 	}
520: 
521: 	err = group.Wait()
522: 	if writeErr := out.Close(); writeErr != nil {
523: 		return writeErr
524: 	}
525: 	if err != nil && !(errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && captureCtx.Err() != nil) {
526: 		return err
527: 	}
528: 
529: 	return nil
530: }

586: // captureChain runs the chained clabwire captures of one group.
587: //
588: // Chaining and the cut: segment k+1 starts `overlap` before segment k is due to end, so both
589: // capture the same packets for a while. clabwire stamps packets when it reads them, so two
590: // processes give the same packet timestamps a few microseconds apart, and timestamps alone
591: // cannot pair them. The chain therefore cuts in the middle of the overlap and matches packets by
592: // content close to the cut:
593: //
594: //  1. When segment k+1 reports Started (pod clock, from its audit record), the cut is
595: //     T = midpoint of [Started(k+1), Started(k) + duration(k)]: both segments run then.
596: //  2. Segment k keeps streaming live, but only packets stamped before T; it remembers the
597: //     content of what it wrote since segment k+1 started.
598: //  3. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. Then the ones stamped
599: //     before T-W are dropped (segment k had them), the ones stamped within W of T are dropped
600: //     when segment k wrote the same bytes on the same interface, and every other one is written.
601: //     From then on segment k+1 streams live.
602: //
603: // Once the pod clock passed T+W, segment k's stdin is closed so it ends without running to its
604: // planned end. While packets are held back, the chain holds the reorder buffer at T-W, so other
605: // nodes' later packets do not overtake them in the merged stream.
606: //
607: // W (500 ms, less for short test segments) covers the stamping difference. Identical frames on
608: // the same interface within W of the cut can be paired with each other, which can drop a true
609: // repeat; nothing else is lost or doubled. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves
610: // a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.
611: type captureChain struct {
612: 	capture *captureRun
613: 	group   *captureGroup
614: 
615: 	events chan segmentEvent
616: 	wg     sync.WaitGroup
617: 
618: 	active *captureSegment
619: 	next   *captureSegment
620: 	// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.
621: 	cut int64
622: 	// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.
623: 	emitted map[uint64]int
624: 	// held are the packets of next until active ends.
625: 	held     []*clabcapture.Packet
626: 	segments int
627: 	retries  int
628: 	// final is set once no further segment is due.
629: 	final bool
630: 	// stopping is set once ctx ended: the segments are asked to end and what they still
631: 	// deliver is written.
632: 	stopping bool
633: }
634: 
635: // run runs the chain until its last segment ended. When ctx ends, it stops the segments and
636: // keeps writing the packets they read until then; a segment that does not end within
637: // captureStdinCloseGrace is cut.
638: func (c *captureChain) run(ctx context.Context) error {
639: 	c.events = make(chan segmentEvent, 256)
640: 	// the segments outlive ctx so they can deliver their last packets; segmentsCtx cuts them
641: 	segmentsCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(ctx))
642: 	var abort *time.Timer
643: 	defer func() {
644: 		if abort != nil {
645: 			abort.Stop()
646: 		}
647: 		cancel()
648: 		c.drain()
649: 		c.capture.out.Release(c)
650: 	}()
651: 
652: 	c.active = c.start(segmentsCtx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
653: 	timer := time.NewTimer(c.nextStartIn())
654: 	defer timer.Stop()
655: 
656: 	done := ctx.Done()
657: 	for {
658: 		select {
659: 		case <-done:
660: 			done = nil
661: 			c.stop(timer)
662: 			abort = time.AfterFunc(captureStdinCloseGrace, cancel)
663: 		case <-segmentsCtx.Done():
664: 			return nil
665: 		case <-timer.C:
666: 			if c.next == nil && !c.final {
667: 				c.startNext(segmentsCtx)
668: 			}
669: 		case event := <-c.events:
670: 			stop, err := c.handle(segmentsCtx, event, timer)
671: 			if err != nil || stop {
672: 				return err
673: 			}
674: 		}
675: 	}
676: }
677: 
678: // stop ends the chain early, like a deadline would: no further segment starts and the running
679: // ones are asked to end. The chain then writes what they deliver until they ended.
680: func (c *captureChain) stop(timer *time.Timer) {
681: 	c.stopping = true
682: 	c.final = true
683: 	timer.Stop()
684: 	c.active.closeStdin()
685: 	if c.next != nil {
686: 		c.next.closeStdin()
687: 	}
688: }
689: 
690: // drain waits for the segment goroutines after the chain ended.
691: func (c *captureChain) drain() {
692: 	done := make(chan struct{})
693: 	go func() {
694: 		c.wg.Wait()
695: 		close(done)
696: 	}()
697: 	for {
698: 		select {
699: 		case <-done:
700: 			return
701: 		case <-c.events:
702: 		}
703: 	}
704: }

706: // segmentDuration is the requested duration of a segment starting now.
707: func (c *captureChain) segmentDuration(now time.Time) time.Duration {
708: 	duration := c.capture.segment
709: 	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() {
710: 		duration = min(duration, c.capture.deadline.Sub(now))
711: 	}
712: 
713: 	return max(duration, minCaptureSegment)
714: }
715: 
716: // nextStartIn is the time until the follow-up of the active segment is due. It marks the chain
717: // final when none is due.
718: func (c *captureChain) nextStartIn() time.Duration {
719: 	if c.stopping {
720: 		c.final = true
721: 		return maxCaptureSegment
722: 	}
723: 	activeEnd := c.active.localStart.Add(c.active.duration)
724: 	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
725: 		!activeEnd.Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
726: 		c.final = true
727: 		return maxCaptureSegment
728: 	}
729: 	c.final = false
730: 
731: 	return max(time.Until(activeEnd.Add(-c.capture.overlap)), 0)
732: }

734: func (c *captureChain) startNext(ctx context.Context) {
735: 	c.next = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
736: 	c.emitted = map[uint64]int{}
737: 	c.held = nil
738: 	c.cut = 0
739: }

741: func (c *captureChain) handle(
742: 	ctx context.Context,
743: 	event segmentEvent,
744: 	timer *time.Timer,
745: ) (bool, error) {
746: 	segment := event.segment
747: 
748: 	switch {
749: 	case event.audit != nil:
750: 		return false, c.handleAudit(segment, event.audit)
751: 	case event.packet != nil:
752: 		return c.handlePacket(segment, event.packet)
753: 	case event.done:
754: 		segment.done = true
755: 		if segment.stopTimer != nil {
756: 			segment.stopTimer.Stop()
757: 		}
758: 		if event.err != nil && !c.stopping {
759: 			if segment == c.next && segment.started.IsZero() && c.retries < captureStartRetries {
760: 				// the follow-up did not start; try again while the active one still runs
761: 				c.retries++
762: 				log.Warn("Capture follow-up segment failed to start, retrying",
763: 					"node", c.group.display, "error", event.err)
764: 				c.next = nil
765: 				resetTimer(timer, time.Second)
766: 
767: 				return false, nil
768: 			}
769: 
770: 			return true, fmt.Errorf("capture on c9s node %s/%s/%s failed: %w",
771: 				c.group.location.Namespace, c.capture.req.Name, c.group.display, event.err)
772: 		}
773: 		if segment != c.active {
774: 			return false, nil
775: 		}
776: 
777: 		return c.switchSegments(ctx, timer)
778: 	}
779: 
780: 	return false, nil
781: }

783: func (c *captureChain) handleAudit(segment *captureSegment, audit *captureAudit) error {
784: 	switch audit.Status {
785: 	case captureAuditStarted:
786: 		segment.started = audit.Time
787: 		log.Debug("Capture segment started", "node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index,
788: 			"interfaces", strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, ","), "duration", segment.duration)
789: 		if segment == c.next && !c.active.started.IsZero() {
790: 			c.setCut()
791: 		}
792: 		if segment == c.next {
793: 			c.retries = 0
794: 		}
795: 	case captureAuditSucceeded:
796: 		segment.ended = audit.Time
797: 		log.Debug("Capture segment succeeded", "node", c.group.display,
798: 			"segment", segment.index, "packets", audit.Packets)
799: 	case captureAuditDenied, captureAuditFailed:
800: 		return captureAuditError(c.group.display, audit)
801: 	}
802: 
803: 	return nil
804: }

806: // captureAuditError turns a Denied or Failed clabwire audit record into an error.
807: func captureAuditError(node string, audit *captureAudit) error {
808: 	verb := "failed"
809: 	if audit.Status == captureAuditDenied {
810: 		verb = "was denied"
811: 	}
812: 	interfaces := make([]string, 0, len(audit.Interfaces))
813: 	for _, intf := range audit.Interfaces {
814: 		interfaces = append(interfaces, intf.Name)
815: 	}
816: 
817: 	return fmt.Errorf("capture of %s on node %s %s by clabwire: %s",
818: 		strings.Join(interfaces, ","), node, verb, audit.Reason)
819: }

821: // setCut places the cut in the middle of the overlap of the active and the next segment, both
822: // measured on the pod clock.
823: func (c *captureChain) setCut() {
824: 	overlapStart := c.next.started
825: 	overlapEnd := c.active.plannedEnd()
826: 	if overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) < 2*c.capture.window {
827: 		// the overlap is too short to match packets around a cut: the switch is reported as a
828: 		// gap once the active segment ended
829: 		c.cut = 0
830: 		return
831: 	}
832: 	c.cut = overlapStart.Add(overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) / 2).UnixNano()
833: 
834: 	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
835: 	// Packets the next segment holds back are stamped from T-W on: other chains' packets after
836: 	// that wait in the reorder buffer until the switch, so the merged stream stays in order.
837: 	c.capture.out.Hold(c, c.cut-window)
838: 
839: 	// The active segment only matters for packets stamped before T. Once the pod clock passed
840: 	// T+W, it is closed: packets it read until then are still delivered, and the ones it reads
841: 	// later are stamped after T and dropped anyway. The next segment's Started record was
842: 	// written on the pod clock no later than now, so the pod clock passes T+W no later than
843: 	// (T - Started + W) from now.
844: 	active := c.active
845: 	active.stopTimer = time.AfterFunc(
846: 		time.Duration(c.cut-c.next.started.UnixNano()+window), active.closeStdin)
847: }

849: func (c *captureChain) handlePacket(
850: 	segment *captureSegment,
851: 	packet *clabcapture.Packet,
852: ) (bool, error) {
853: 	switch segment {
854: 	case c.active:
855: 		if c.cut != 0 && packet.Timestamp >= c.cut {
856: 			return false, nil
857: 		}
858: 		if c.next != nil {
859: 			c.emitted[packetKey(packet)]++
860: 		}
861: 
862: 		return c.emit(packet)
863: 	case c.next:
864: 		c.held = append(c.held, packet)
865: 	}
866: 
867: 	return false, nil
868: }
869: 
870: func (c *captureChain) emit(packet *clabcapture.Packet) (bool, error) {
871: 	if int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(c.group.ids) {
872: 		return true, fmt.Errorf("clabwire wrote a packet for interface %d of %d",
873: 			packet.InterfaceID, len(c.group.ids))
874: 	}
875: 	more, err := c.capture.emit(c.group.ids[packet.InterfaceID], packet)
876: 
877: 	return !more, err
878: }

880: // switchSegments makes the next segment the active one after the active one ended, writing the
881: // held packets of the next one that the active one did not write.
882: func (c *captureChain) switchSegments(ctx context.Context, timer *time.Timer) (bool, error) {
883: 	// the held packets are in the reorder buffer once this returns
884: 	defer c.capture.out.Release(c)
885: 
886: 	ended := c.active
887: 	if c.stopping && c.next != nil && c.next.started.IsZero() {
888: 		// the chain is stopping: a follow-up that has not started takes nothing over
889: 		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
890: 	}
891: 	if c.final && c.next == nil {
892: 		return true, nil
893: 	}
894: 
895: 	if c.next == nil || c.next.started.IsZero() || c.cut == 0 {
896: 		from := ended.ended
897: 		if from.IsZero() {
898: 			from = ended.plannedEnd()
899: 		}
900: 		gap := clablabruntime.CaptureGap{
901: 			Node: c.group.display, Interfaces: c.group.interfaces, From: from,
902: 			Reason: "the follow-up capture did not overlap the previous one",
903: 		}
904: 		if c.next != nil && !c.next.started.IsZero() {
905: 			gap.To = c.next.started
906: 		}
907: 		c.capture.reportGap(gap)
908: 	}
909: 
910: 	if c.next != nil && c.next.done && !c.stopping {
911: 		// the follow-up already ended (it started too late to take over): keep what it
912: 		// captured and continue with a fresh segment
913: 		for _, packet := range c.held {
914: 			if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
915: 				return true, err
916: 			}
917: 		}
918: 		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
919: 	}
920: 
921: 	if c.next == nil {
922: 		if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
923: 			!time.Now().Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
924: 			return true, nil
925: 		}
926: 		c.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
927: 		resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
928: 
929: 		return false, nil
930: 	}
931: 
932: 	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
933: 	for _, packet := range c.held {
934: 		if c.cut != 0 {
935: 			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut-window {
936: 				continue
937: 			}
938: 			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut+window {
939: 				key := packetKey(packet)
940: 				if c.emitted[key] > 0 {
941: 					c.emitted[key]--
942: 					continue
943: 				}
944: 			}
945: 		}
946: 		if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
947: 			return true, err
948: 		}
949: 	}
950: 
951: 	c.active, c.next = c.next, nil
952: 	c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, 0
953: 	if c.active.done {
954: 		// the chain is stopping and the follow-up ended before the active one
955: 		return true, nil
956: 	}
957: 	resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
958: 
959: 	return false, nil
960: }

962: func resetTimer(timer *time.Timer, d time.Duration) {
963: 	if !timer.Stop() {
964: 		select {
965: 		case <-timer.C:
966: 		default:
967: 		}
968: 	}
969: 	timer.Reset(d)
970: }

972: // packetKey identifies a packet by its interface and content.
973: func packetKey(packet *clabcapture.Packet) uint64 {
974: 	hash := fnv.New64a()
975: 	var id [4]byte
976: 	id[0] = byte(packet.InterfaceID)
977: 	id[1] = byte(packet.InterfaceID >> 8)
978: 	_, _ = hash.Write(id[:])
979: 	_, _ = hash.Write(packet.Data)
980: 
981: 	return hash.Sum64()
982: }
